questions.question: Which irrigation system is commonly used in arid regions of India to conserve water by directly delivering irrigation water to the roots of plants?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Drip irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Drip irrigation** is a micro-irrigation system designed to save water and nutrients by allowing water to drip slowly to the roots of plants.
 
• This system is ideal for **arid and semi-arid regions**, where water conservation is critical.
 
• The water is delivered through a network of valves, pipes, tubing, and emitters, ensuring precise delivery directly to the plant's root zone.

questions.question: Which zone of the Great Indian Plains has high humidity and marshy conditions?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Terai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Terai region** is a marshy and humid zone located in the **Great Indian Plains**, situated along the foothills of the **Himalayas**.
 
• It is characterized by **high groundwater levels** due to frequent seepage from rivers descending from the Himalayas.
 
• The region is known for its **dense forests** and fertile land, making it an agriculturally productive area.
 
• The **climatic conditions** in the Terai are humid, with significant rainfall, contributing to its marshy characteristics.
 
• The Terai serves as an important **wildlife habitat**, home to species like the Bengal tiger, rhinoceros, and elephants, particularly in areas like the **Terai Arc Landscape**.
 
• It is a transitional area between the **plains** and the **mountains**, and its geographical features play a critical role in the hydrology of northern India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhabar**__

 __
 
• The **Bhabar** zone lies just above the Terai region, at the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• It is characterized by a **porous and rocky terrain**, which causes rivers to disappear underground.
 
• The soil in this region is less fertile, and agriculture is limited.
 
 
 
• **Bhangar**__
 __
 
• **Bhangar** refers to the **older alluvial soil** found in the Great Indian Plains.
 
• This area is slightly elevated and less fertile compared to the newer alluvial soil (Khadar).
 
• It is primarily used for **pasture and settlement** rather than intensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Delta**__
 
 
• The **Delta** region is located at the mouths of major rivers like the Ganga and Brahmaputra.
 
• It is characterized by extremely fertile soil, making it one of the most productive agricultural zones in India.
 
• This region often experiences **flooding** and is rich in biodiversity.

questions.question: Which of the following farming techniques is primarily practised by tribal groups in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shifting agriculture**, also known as "slash-and-burn agriculture," is a traditional farming technique practised by tribal groups in India.
 
• In this method, patches of forest land are cleared by cutting and burning trees, and the land is used for cultivation until its fertility decreases.
 
• It is primarily practised in hilly and forested regions such as the northeastern states of India (e.g., Nagaland, Mizoram, and Manipur) and parts of Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Shifting agriculture is a subsistence farming method, meaning it is done primarily to meet the needs of the farmer's family rather than for commercial purposes.
 
• After a few years of cultivation, the land is left fallow for natural vegetation to grow back, which helps restore soil fertility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Agriculture in India**

 
 
• **Commercial farming:** Involves large-scale production of crops for sale in markets (e.g., sugarcane, cotton).
 
• **Intensive farming:** High inputs of labor and capital are used on smaller plots of land to maximize output.
 
• **Plantation farming:** Large-scale cultivation of a single crop like tea, coffee, or rubber, typically for export.
 
 
 
• **Jhum Cultivation:** A specific form of shifting agriculture practised in northeastern India, where tribal farmers cultivate crops like rice, maize, and millets on cleared forest patches.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Shifting agriculture can lead to deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity if not practised sustainably.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Efforts are being made to introduce alternative livelihood options and sustainable farming practices for tribal communities to reduce the environmental impact of shifting agriculture.
 
• **Alternative Names:** Shifting agriculture is also referred to as "jhum," "podu," or "bewar" in different regions of India.

questions.question: Most of the Thar Desert lies in which direction with respect to the Aravalli Hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-West**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert is geographically located to the **North-West of the Aravalli Hills**, which act as a natural barrier influencing its climatic conditions.
 
• The Aravalli Hills, one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, run from northeast to southwest across northwestern India.
 
• The orientation of the Aravalli Hills significantly affects the wind patterns, leading to the accumulation of desert sand towards the North-West region.
 
• The Thar Desert spans across the Indian states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, with a major portion lying in Rajasthan.
 
• The desert's proximity to the Aravalli Hills helps restrict the eastward expansion of the sandy terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is the 17th largest desert in the world and the 9th largest subtropical desert.
 
• It covers an area of approximately 200,000 square kilometers, making it the most densely populated desert in the world.
 
• The desert is characterized by extreme temperatures, scarce vegetation, and low precipitation (100-500 mm annually).
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Hills:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills are a range of ancient fold mountains extending approximately 692 kilometers across northwest India.
 
• They play a crucial role in determining the local climate and act as a protective barrier against desertification to the east.
 
• The highest peak is Guru Shikhar, located in Mount Abu, Rajasthan, at an elevation of 1,722 meters.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Influence:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills influence the monsoon winds, causing the western region to remain arid while the eastern plains receive moderate rainfall.
 
• The desert's location to the northwest of the hills results in its characteristic dry and sandy climate.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna:**
 
 
• The desert supports various drought-resistant plants such as cacti, acacia, and khejri trees.
 
• Wildlife includes species like the Indian gazelle (chinkara), desert fox, and great Indian bustard, which are adapted to arid conditions.

questions.question: The longitudinal valleys between the lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Duns**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Duns** are longitudinal valleys situated between the **Lesser Himalayas** (or Middle Himalayas) and the **Shiwalik** range.
 
• They are formed due to the folding of sedimentary rocks during the Himalayan orogeny (mountain-building process).
 
• Examples of prominent duns include **Dehradun**, **Kotli Dun**, and **Patli Dun**.
 
• These valleys are often fertile and support agriculture, making them important for the local economy.
 
• The term "dun" is derived from the Hindi word “doon,” which means a valley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lesser Himalayas:**

 
 
• The Lesser Himalayas, also called the **Himachal**, are located north of the Shiwaliks and south of the Greater Himalayas.
 
• They are composed of metamorphic and sedimentary rocks and are known for their rugged terrain and deep valleys.
 
 
 
• **Shiwalik Range:**
 
 
• The Shiwaliks are the outermost range of the Himalayas and are made up of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• This range is prone to erosion and is characterized by steep slopes.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Orogeny:**
 
 
• The Himalayas were formed due to the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate around 50 million years ago.
 
• This tectonic activity caused the folding and upliftment of sedimentary rocks, leading to the formation of ranges and valleys like duns.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Valleys:**
 
 
• **Doabs:** Land between two rivers, typically used in the Indo-Gangetic Plains (e.g., Punjab's doabs).
 
• **Meanders:** Curved bends in a river channel, primarily formed in its lower course.
 
• **Khadars:** Fertile alluvial soil regions formed by river deposition during floods, often found in the Indo-Gangetic Plains.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak of the Maikal range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amarkantak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amarkantak** is the highest peak of the Maikal range, located in the Vindhya-Satpura region in Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It is situated at an altitude of approximately **1,048 meters (3,438 feet)** above sea level.
 
• Amarkantak is also known as the **"Teerthraj"** or the "King of Pilgrimage" due to its religious significance.
 
• The **Narmada River**, one of the most sacred rivers in India, originates from this peak.
 
• This region is also an ecologically significant area, home to rich biodiversity and dense forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maikal Range:**

 
 
• The Maikal range is a part of the Satpura Hills, located in central India, covering parts of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It acts as the connecting link between the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges.
 
• The range is characterized by its undulating terrain, forests, and rich mineral resources.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River:**
 
 
• The Narmada River is one of the seven sacred rivers of India, originating from Amarkantak.
 
• It flows westward, unlike most Indian rivers, which flow eastward.
 
• The river is vital for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric projects in central India.
 
 
 
• **Religious Importance of Amarkantak:**
 
 
• Amarkantak is a popular pilgrimage site for Hindus, with temples dedicated to Lord Shiva and Goddess Narmada.
 
• It is believed that the meeting of the Vindhya and Satpura ranges at Amarkantak has spiritual significance.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Significance:**
 
 
• The forests of the Maikal range are part of the Eastern Highlands Moist Deciduous Forests ecoregion.
 
• The region is home to a variety of wildlife, including leopards, bears, and numerous bird species.

questions.question: Which of the following states is famous for its ingenious water conservation methods, 'taanka' or 'kunds'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rajasthan** is renowned for its traditional water conservation systems, especially **'taanka'** and **'kunds'**, which are designed to store rainwater efficiently.
 
• 'Kunds' are circular underground structures with sloping roofs that collect rainwater, making them ideal for arid regions.
 
• 'Taanka' is a technique used to store water in small tanks, usually found near households, ensuring water availability during dry seasons.
 
• These systems are vital in Rajasthan's desert climate, which experiences low and erratic rainfall, emphasizing the need for sustainable water management.
 
• Such indigenous methods highlight Rajasthan's commitment to water conservation and its cultural heritage of managing scarce resources effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Conservation Techniques in India:**

 
 
• India employs several traditional water conservation methods, such as **stepwells (baolis)**, **johads**, and **check dams**.
 
• These techniques are tailored to specific climatic and geographical conditions.
 
 
 
• **Rainwater Harvesting:**
 
 
• A modern adaptation of traditional systems, rainwater harvesting involves collecting and storing rainwater for domestic and agricultural use.
 
• It is widely promoted in India to address water scarcity issues, particularly in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Desert Climate of Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan is characterized by extreme temperatures, low rainfall (average annual rainfall of 100-400 mm), and arid conditions.
 
• Indigenous water conservation systems like 'kunds' and 'taankas' have played a pivotal role in sustaining life in such challenging environments.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance of Water Conservation:**
 
 
• Traditional water systems like 'kunds' have been used for centuries and are examples of sustainable development practices.
 
• They showcase the ingenuity of communities in adapting to harsh climates while preserving resources.

questions.question: What is the dominant soil type in the Great Plains of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the dominant soil type found in the Great Plains of India.
 
• It is formed by the deposition of silt, sand, and clay brought down by rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.
 
• The Great Plains are a part of the Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra plain, which is one of the most fertile regions in the world.
 
• Alluvial soils in the region are highly suitable for agriculture, supporting the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
• These soils are rich in nutrients such as potash and lime but are generally deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• It is categorized into two types: **Khadar (new alluvium)**, which is found closer to riverbanks, and **Bhangar (old alluvium)**, located farther from rivers.
 
• Khadar soils are more fertile due to frequent river depositions, while Bhangar soils contain kankar (calcareous concretions).
 
 
 
• **Formation of Alluvial Soil:** This soil is formed by the action of rivers and is transported and deposited over time, creating extensive plains and deltas.
 
• **Distribution in India:** Alluvial soils are extensively found in the northern plains, including Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal, and along river valleys in other parts of the country.
 
• **Agricultural Importance:** Due to their fine texture, good water-retention capacity, and nutrient content, alluvial soils are considered ideal for intensive agricultural activities.
 
• **Soil Management:** Regular use of fertilizers and crop rotation practices are necessary to replenish nutrients and maintain soil fertility.

questions.question: Kanpur, a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, is an example of which type of town?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial Town**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanpur**, located in Uttar Pradesh, is one of the prominent **industrial towns** in India.
 
• It is known for its **textile, leather, and chemical industries**, which contribute significantly to its economy.
 
• During British rule, Kanpur was a major center for **cotton and woolen textiles**, earning it the nickname "Manchester of the East."
 
• The city's **leather industry** is globally recognized, making Kanpur a significant hub for leather goods production and export.
 
• Kanpur hosts several industrial estates, fostering growth in **engineering, fertilizers, and plastics** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Town:**

 
 
• It refers to a city or town primarily focused on **industrial production and manufacturing**.
 
• Such towns typically have **factories, warehouses, and industrial estates** as their key features.
 
• These towns often experience rapid urbanization due to **employment opportunities** in the industrial sector.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Towns:**
 
 
• **Administrative Towns:** Serve as centers for governmental administration, e.g., New Delhi.
 
• **Recreational Towns:** Focus on tourism and leisure, e.g., Shimla.
 
• **Transfer and Distribution Towns:** Act as hubs for trade and transportation, e.g., Varanasi.
 
 
 
• **Leather Industry in Kanpur:**
 
 
• Kanpur's leather industry is one of the largest in India, producing **shoes, belts, bags, and saddlery goods**.
 
• The city exports leather products to the USA, UK, and other countries, contributing to India's foreign exchange earnings.
 
 
 
• **Manchester of the East:**
 
 
• Kanpur earned this title due to its **significant role in textile production** during the British era.
 
• The city hosted major textile mills such as **Lal Imli Woolen Mills** and **Elgin Mills**.

questions.question: Convectional rainfall is common in which part of India during the pre-monsoon period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhota Nagpur Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Convectional rainfall occurs due to intense heating of the earth's surface, causing warm air to rise, cool, and condense to form precipitation.
 
• In India, this phenomenon is common during the pre-monsoon period in regions like the **Chhota Nagpur Plateau**, especially in summer.
 
• This region experiences high temperatures during the pre-monsoon months (March to May), which leads to the formation of cumulus clouds and subsequent rainfall.
 
• The rainfall is often accompanied by thunderstorms and is locally known as **"Nor'westers" or "Kal Baisakhi"** in eastern India.
 
• These rains are vital for agriculture in the region, especially for crops like rice and maize.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convectional Rainfall:**

 
 
• This type of rainfall occurs when the sun heats the earth's surface intensely, causing moisture-laden air to rise rapidly.
 
• As the air rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds, eventually leading to precipitation.
 
• It is most common in equatorial regions but can also occur in specific areas during summer months.
 
 
 
• **Chhota Nagpur Plateau:**
 
 
• Located in eastern India, covering parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• Known for its rich mineral resources and dense forest cover.
 
• The plateau experiences extreme weather conditions, including hot summers and convectional rains during pre-monsoon periods.
 
 
 
• **Nor'westers (Kal Baisakhi):**
 
 
• These are violent local storms accompanied by strong winds, rain, and occasional hail.
 
• They are common in eastern India, especially in West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha, during the pre-monsoon season.
 
• The term "Kal Baisakhi" translates to "Calamity of Baisakh" (a month in the Hindu calendar).
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**
 
 
• The convectional rainfall during the pre-monsoon period provides crucial water for kharif crops.
 
• The accompanying thunderstorms can sometimes damage standing crops due to hail or strong winds.

questions.question: Which of the following features is NOT typical of the Thar Desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dense evergreen forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is characterized by arid and semi-arid conditions, making it unsuitable for the growth of dense evergreen forests.
 
• Typical features of the Thar Desert include **shifting sand dunes**, which are formed by strong winds common in the region.
 
• **Inland drainage** is a key feature, where rivers like Luni do not reach the sea but instead terminate in saline lakes or disappear into the ground.
 
• **Oases** are scattered across the desert and serve as vital sources of water and vegetation for local populations and wildlife.
 
• The absence of dense vegetation, including evergreen forests, is due to the extreme climatic conditions, such as high temperatures and low rainfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert Geography**

 
 
• It spans across northwestern India and eastern Pakistan, covering an area of approximately 200,000 square kilometers.
 
• It is bounded by the Aravalli Hills in the east, the Indus River in the west, and the Rann of Kutch in the south.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Conditions**
 
 
• The desert experiences extreme temperatures, ranging from 0°C in winter to over 50°C in summer.
 
• Annual rainfall is sparse, typically less than 200 mm, contributing to its arid environment.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**
 
 
• Vegetation is sparse and consists mainly of shrubs, thorny bushes, and xerophytes adapted to arid conditions.
 
• Common wildlife includes camels, blackbucks, desert foxes, and various species of lizards and snakes.
 
 
 
• **Human Adaptations**
 
 
• The local population relies on traditional water conservation methods such as step wells and tankas to survive.
 
• The region's economy is supported by agriculture, livestock rearing, and salt mining in saline areas.

questions.question: Which latitude passes through the Rann of Kutch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23.5ºN**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tropic of Cancer, located at 23.5ºN latitude, passes through the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, India.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer is one of Earth's major latitude lines, marking the northernmost point of the Sun's zenith during the summer solstice.
 
• India is one of the 16 countries through which the Tropic of Cancer passes, and it cuts across eight Indian states, including Gujarat.
 
• The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh located in the Thar Desert region of Gujarat and is geographically significant due to its proximity to the Tropic of Cancer.
 
• This latitude plays a crucial role in the climatic variations and geographical positioning of the regions it crosses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropic of Cancer:**

 
 
• The Tropic of Cancer is an imaginary line situated at 23.5ºN latitude, marking the boundary of the Earth's northern tropical zone.
 
• During the summer solstice (around June 21), the Sun is directly overhead at this latitude, making it a crucial marker in Earth's solar system dynamics.
 
• This latitude influences the climatic conditions of the regions it crosses, including arid zones and monsoon patterns.
 
 
 
• **Rann of Kutch:**
 
 
• The Rann of Kutch spans across Gujarat, India, and extends into Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• It is one of the largest salt deserts in the world, covering an area of approximately 10,000 square kilometers.
 
• The region is famous for the annual Rann Utsav, showcasing the rich culture and heritage of Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Influence of Tropic of Cancer:**
 
 
• Regions close to the Tropic of Cancer experience tropical and subtropical climates.
 
• The latitude influences rainfall patterns, leading to distinct wet and dry seasons in many areas.
 
• It plays a role in agricultural practices due to its climatic impact on soil and vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Importance:**
 
 
• Countries through which the Tropic of Cancer passes include India, Mexico, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and others.
 
• Its passage through India makes it a vital reference for geographical studies and climatic assessments.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer marks the northern limit of the tropical zone, separating it from the temperate zone.

questions.question: Which of the following urban agglomerations has the highest population in India as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Census 2011, **Mumbai** is the most populous urban agglomeration in India.
 
• Mumbai's urban agglomeration had a population of approximately **18.4 million** in 2011.
 
• Mumbai, often referred to as the financial capital of India, attracts people from across the country due to its economic opportunities.
 
• Other major urban agglomerations include Delhi (16.3 million), Kolkata (14.1 million), and Bengaluru (8.5 million).
 
• Mumbai's metropolitan region includes areas such as Thane, Navi Mumbai, and Vasai-Virar, contributing to its high population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Agglomeration:**

 
 
• An urban agglomeration refers to a continuously built-up area consisting of a city and its adjoining towns.
 
• It often includes areas beyond the municipal boundaries of the main city, forming a larger metropolitan region.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• The Census 2011 was India's 15th National Census, conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner.
 
• It provided comprehensive demographic, economic, and social data for policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Population Density of Mumbai:**
 
 
• Mumbai is one of the most densely populated cities in the world, with a density of over **20,000 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Its high population density is attributed to factors such as economic opportunities, migration, and limited land availability.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance of Mumbai:**
 
 
• Mumbai is home to major financial institutions like the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), and corporate headquarters.
 
• It also hosts Bollywood, India's largest film industry, contributing significantly to the city's economy.

questions.question: Which major port is NOT located on the western coast of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Visakhapatnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Visakhapatnam Port** is located on the eastern coast of India, along the Bay of Bengal, in the state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is one of the oldest ports in India, operational since 1933, and plays a key role in maritime trade on the eastern coast.
 
• Major ports like **Kandla, Cochin, and Mangalore** are situated on the western coast of India, facing the Arabian Sea.
 
• The western coast of India is known for its other important ports such as **Mumbai Port** and **Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva)**.
 
• Visakhapatnam Port serves as a major hub for cargo handling, especially coal, petroleum products, and iron ore, on the eastern seaboard of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Ports in India**

 
 
• India has 13 major ports divided between the eastern and western coasts.
 
• Western coast ports include Kandla, Mumbai, Mangalore, Cochin, and Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva).
 
• Eastern coast ports include Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Kolkata (Haldia), and Chennai.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Visakhapatnam Port**
 
 
• It is a natural harbor and one of the deepest ports in India.
 
• It is a key gateway for exports and imports for central and eastern India.
 
• It houses a major shipyard and serves as a base for the Indian Navy's Eastern Command.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features of India's Coastline**
 
 
• The western coastline runs along the Arabian Sea and includes states like Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The eastern coastline runs along the Bay of Bengal and includes states like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• The western coast is characterized by estuaries and lagoons, whereas the eastern coast has deltas formed by major rivers like the Ganges, Godavari, and Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Port Development in India**
 
 
• The Indian government launched the **Sagarmala Project** to modernize port infrastructure and enhance connectivity.
 
• Major ports are governed by the **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**, which aims to increase their efficiency and autonomy.

questions.question: The crescent-shaped sand dunes found in the Thar Desert are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barchans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Barchans** are crescent-shaped sand dunes found in arid and semi-arid regions, such as the Thar Desert in India.
 
• They are formed due to the action of **unidirectional winds** that move loose sand particles.
 
• The horns of a barchan point in the direction of the wind, while the steep slip face lies on the leeward side.
 
• These dunes are typically found in areas with **limited vegetation**, which allows wind to transport sand freely.
 
• Barchans are a common feature of deserts worldwide, including the Sahara Desert and the Arabian Desert, apart from the Thar Desert.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ergs:**

 
 
• An erg is a vast area covered with loose sand and characterized by sand dunes.
 
• It is also known as a "sand sea" and is typically found in large desert systems like the Sahara.
 
 
 
• **Inselbergs:**
 
 
• An inselberg is an isolated hill or mountain that rises abruptly from a plain.
 
• It is formed due to the erosion of surrounding softer rock, leaving behind hard rock masses.
 
 
 
• **Yardangs:**
 
 
• Yardangs are streamlined, wind-eroded ridges of rock that are aligned with the prevailing wind direction.
 
• They are formed in areas where the rock is soft and easily eroded, leaving behind elongated ridges.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Sand Dunes:**
 
 
• Sand dunes are formed by the accumulation of sand grains transported by wind through processes like **saltation, suspension, and surface creep**.
 
• The shape and size of dunes depend on wind speed, direction, and the availability of sand.

questions.question: Which soil is deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus but rich in iron and aluminium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laterite Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Laterite soil** is formed under high temperature and heavy rainfall, leading to intense leaching of soil nutrients.
 
• This soil is **deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium**, making it less fertile for agricultural purposes.
 
• It is rich in **iron oxide and aluminium**, giving it a distinct reddish or brown color.
 
• Laterite soil is commonly found in regions like **Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and parts of Maharashtra, Odisha, Kerala, and Karnataka.**
 
• It is widely used for **brick-making and construction material** due to its compact and hard nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leaching Process:**

 
 
• Leaching occurs due to heavy rainfall washing away soluble nutrients like nitrogen and potassium from the soil.
 
• This process leaves behind insoluble oxides like iron and aluminium, which dominate laterite soil composition.
 
 
 
• **Formation Conditions:**
 
 
• Laterite soil forms in tropical and subtropical regions with alternating wet and dry climates.
 
• The intense weathering of parent rock contributes to its unique mineral composition.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• It is extensively used in **brick-making** for construction purposes.
 
• In agriculture, it is suitable for crops like cashew, coffee, and tea with proper soil management.
 
 
 
• **Distribution in India:**
 
 
• Laterite soil is predominantly found in states such as **Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and Odisha.**
 
• It covers nearly 2.48 lakh square kilometers of land in India.

questions.question: The McMahon Line separates India from which country?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **McMahon Line** is the boundary line that separates **India** from **China**.
 
• It was drawn during the **Simla Convention** of **1914**, between British India and Tibet, with the presence of China.
 
• The line is named after **Sir Henry McMahon**, the then Foreign Secretary of British India, who represented India in the negotiations.
 
• This line is situated in the northeastern region of India, specifically along the state of **Arunachal Pradesh**, which China often claims as part of its territory.
 
• The McMahon Line runs for approximately **550 miles** (885 kilometers).
 
• While India recognizes the McMahon Line as its legal boundary, **China disputes** this line, leading to border tensions between the two nations.
 
• The region around the McMahon Line is geopolitically sensitive and has been the site of conflicts, including the **Sino-Indian War of 1962**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pakistan**__

 __
 
• India shares its western border with **Pakistan**, marked primarily by the **Radcliffe Line**.
 
• The **Radcliffe Line** was drawn during the **partition of India** in **1947**.
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is highly sensitive, with disputes over regions such as **Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Nepal**__
 __
 
• India shares an open border with **Nepal**, which is marked by the **Mahakali River** in certain regions.
 
• The **India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950)** governs the bilateral relationship between the two countries.
 
• Citizens of both countries can travel across the border without requiring a visa or passport.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan**__
 
 
• India shares its northeastern border with **Bhutan**.
 
• The border is defined by geographical features such as the **Himalayas**.
 
• India and Bhutan maintain strong diplomatic ties, and India assists Bhutan in its development projects.

questions.question: Which of the following countries DOES NOT share a land boundary with India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sri Lanka** is an island nation located in the **Indian Ocean**, southeast of India.
 
• It does not share a **land boundary** with India. Instead, it is separated from India by the **Palk Strait** and the **Gulf of Mannar.**
 
• The shortest distance between India and Sri Lanka is approximately **30 km**, across the **Adam's Bridge (Rama's Bridge or Ram Setu).**
 
• Although there is no land boundary, the two nations share **historical, cultural, and economic ties.**
 
• Sri Lanka is often referred to as the **"Pearl of the Indian Ocean"** due to its unique shape and strategic location.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Myanmar**__

 __
 
• **Myanmar** shares a **land boundary** with India along the northeastern region.
 
• The border length between India and Myanmar is approximately **1,643 km**.
 
• Four Indian states share borders with Myanmar: **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.**
 
• Myanmar is a part of the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)**, which includes India as well.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan**__
 __
 
• **Bhutan** is a landlocked country in the **Himalayan region** and shares a **land boundary** with India.
 
• The India-Bhutan border is approximately **699 km** long.
 
• Indian states sharing borders with Bhutan include **Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, West Bengal, and Sikkim.**
 
• The relationship between India and Bhutan is guided by the **Treaty of Friendship (1949, revised in 2007).**
 
 
 
• **Afghanistan**__
 
 
• **Afghanistan** shares a **land boundary** with India at the **northeastern tip of Jammu and Kashmir** (now part of Ladakh under Indian administration) through the **Wakhan Corridor.**
 
• The **Durand Line** separates Afghanistan from Pakistan, and indirectly, it has implications for the Indian border.
 
• However, the region near the India-Afghanistan border is remote and sparsely populated.

__

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the nature of the Northern Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial and fertile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plain** of India is primarily composed of **alluvial soil**, deposited by three major river systems: the **Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers**.
 
• This plain is one of the most **fertile and agriculturally productive regions** in the world.
 
• The fertile soil supports the growth of a variety of crops, including **wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses**.
 
• The alluvial deposits in this region are a result of **continuous sedimentation** over millions of years.
 
• The plain covers a vast area, stretching across the states of **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam**.
 
• It is divided into three main sections: the **Punjab Plains, Ganga Plains, and Brahmaputra Plains**, each named after the dominant river system in the respective area.
 
• The region is densely populated due to its **fertile land, availability of water, and favorable climatic conditions**.
 
• The alluvial soil in the Northern Plain is rich in **minerals like potash and lime**, making it ideal for agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hilly and forested**__

 __
 
• This term refers to regions that have **elevated terrain and dense vegetation**, such as the **Himalayas** or the **Western Ghats**.
 
• The Northern Plain, however, is a **flat and level region**, making this option incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Rocky and elevated**__
 __
 
• Rocky and elevated regions are characteristic of **plateaus or mountainous areas**, such as the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• The Northern Plain, being formed by river deposits, is **flat and not rocky or elevated**.
 
 
 
• **Arid and barren**__
 
 
• This term describes **dry and infertile regions** such as the **Thar Desert** in Rajasthan.
 
• The Northern Plain, by contrast, is known for its **fertile soil and abundant water resources**, making this option unsuitable.

questions.question: Which of the following soils is most suitable for rice cultivation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the most suitable soil for rice cultivation due to its **fertility and moisture retention capacity**.
 
• It is rich in essential nutrients such as **potash, phosphoric acid, and lime**, which are required for the growth of rice plants.
 
• Alluvial soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers such as the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus**.
 
• This soil type is widely found in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, which is a major rice-growing region in India.
 
• It has a **clayey texture** that helps retain water, a crucial factor for rice cultivation as rice requires standing water during its growth phase.
 
• Alluvial soil is found in **low-lying areas** that are naturally irrigated by river systems, making it ideal for rice farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Desert Soil**__

 __
 
• **Desert soil** is found in arid regions such as **Rajasthan** and is characterized by low fertility and high sand content.
 
• It lacks moisture and organic content, making it unsuitable for rice cultivation.
 
• This soil type is typically used for crops that require minimal water, such as **millets and pulses**.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**__
 __
 
• **Red soil** is found in regions such as **Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka**.
 
• It is formed by the weathering of crystalline rocks and is rich in **iron oxide**, giving it a reddish color.
 
• Although it is fertile for crops like **groundnut, cotton, and millets**, it lacks essential nutrients such as nitrogen and organic matter, making it less suitable for rice cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Saline Soil**__
 
 
• **Saline soil** is characterized by high salt content and is found in areas such as **Rann of Kutch in Gujarat and coastal regions**.
 
• It is not suitable for most crops, including rice, due to its **poor drainage and high salinity**.
 
• Efforts are often required to reclaim saline soils for agricultural use.

questions.question: The Thar Desert is classified as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

The correct answer is __**Subtropical Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is classified as a **subtropical desert** due to its location and climatic conditions.
 
• It is located in the northwestern part of India and eastern Pakistan, covering an area of approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• Subtropical deserts are characterized by **high temperatures during the day**, cooler nights, and **low annual rainfall**.
 
• The Thar Desert receives an annual rainfall of less than **200 mm**, making it one of the driest regions in India.
 
• Its climate is influenced by the **Hadley cell circulation**, which creates stable, dry air masses over subtropical latitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subtropical Desert Characteristics**

 
 
• Subtropical deserts are located between **20° and 30° north or south latitude**.
 
• They have **hot summers** with temperatures often exceeding 40°C.
 
• Rainfall is scarce, often occurring in brief, sporadic showers.
 
• Vegetation is sparse and adapted to drought conditions.
 
 
 
• **Geography of the Thar Desert**
 
 
• It covers parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana in India and Sindh in Pakistan.
 
• The desert is home to unique sand dune formations and salt marshes like the **Rann of Kutch**.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**
 
 
• Vegetation includes drought-resistant shrubs, grasses, and **acacia trees**.
 
• Wildlife includes species like desert foxes, camels, and the endangered **Great Indian Bustard**.
 
 
 
• **Human Settlement**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.
 
• Communities rely on agriculture, animal husbandry, and tourism for their livelihoods.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates in the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Krishna River originates in the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is one of the longest rivers in India, with a total length of approximately **1,400 km**, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The river flows eastward and empties into the Bay of Bengal, supporting agriculture and irrigation along its course.
 
• Key tributaries of the Krishna River include the **Tungabhadra, Koyna, and Bhima Rivers**, among others.
 
• The Krishna River basin is known for its fertile lands and is a vital water source for millions in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**

 
 
• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India, known for their biodiversity and ecological significance.
 
• They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major source of many important rivers in peninsular India.
 
 
 
• **Major Rivers Originating in the Western Ghats:**
 
 
• Besides Krishna, other important rivers originating from the Western Ghats include the Godavari, Kaveri, and Periyar.
 
• These rivers are crucial for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation in the southern states of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Krishna River:**
 
 
• The Krishna River is essential for agriculture, providing irrigation to large areas in the Deccan Plateau.
 
• It supports several major dams and irrigation projects, such as the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam and the Srisailam Dam.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Concerns:**
 
 
• Like many rivers in India, the Krishna River faces challenges such as pollution, over-extraction of water, and reduced flow due to climate change.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve and sustainably manage the river and its basin.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of contract farming in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fixed buy-back rate by companies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Contract farming** involves an agreement between a farmer and a company (buyer) for the production and supply of agricultural products at predetermined prices.
 
• The agreement often includes a **fixed buy-back rate** for the produce, ensuring price stability for the farmers.
 
• It is a practice widely adopted to **reduce market risks for farmers** and ensure a steady supply of raw materials for companies.
 
• Contract farming provides access to **advanced technology, quality seeds, fertilizers, and technical knowledge** supplied by companies.
 
• It is a regulated practice under the **Indian Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Contract Farming Act, 2018**, which protects the interests of both farmers and companies.

• **Contract Farming Act, 2018:**

 
 
• This model act aims to promote contract farming by providing a framework for agreements between farmers and sponsors.
 
• It includes provisions to prevent exploitation of farmers, including **no transfer of land ownership** to sponsors.
 
• The act also ensures dispute resolution through a fast-track mechanism.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Contract Farming:**
 
 
• Farmers benefit from guaranteed pricing and reduced market risks.
 
• Companies ensure a steady supply of raw materials with desired quality standards.
 
• Farmers gain access to modern technology and better farming practices.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Contract Farming:**
 
 
• Farmers may become overly dependent on companies for inputs and technology.
 
• Disputes may arise regarding quality standards, payment delays, or pricing.
 
• Small farmers may face challenges in negotiating favorable contract terms.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Contract Farming in India:**
 
 
• PepsiCo's potato farming initiative in Punjab for its snack products.
 
• Nestle's milk procurement model through direct contracts with dairy farmers.
 
• ITC's e-Choupal initiative for sourcing agricultural produce directly from farmers.
